## Bounded browser refresh batching

- High-volume per-VPS WebSocket events are now invalidation hints rather than
  one database refresh trigger per event. Telemetry uses the existing
  15-second fleet cadence; agent, job-output, per-target job-finished, and
  backup-artifact waves share one fixed 15-second browser refresh batch.
- The batch window does not reset when more events arrive, so sustained traffic
  cannot postpone updates indefinitely. Agent changes request one full fleet
  snapshot at the next cadence, and concurrent dirty job IDs are retained so a
  selected job's output evidence is not lost behind another job.
- The focused browser stress exercised more than 1,800 mixed WebSocket events
  across 100 rotating VPS identities. It produced no database-backed refresh
  before the first boundary and exactly four refresh groups during the measured
  minute, including full fleet, jobs, selected-job detail, inventory, audit,
  and backup evidence.

## Scope

- This is a frontend refresh-policy correction. WebSocket and REST schemas,
  agent/gateway command protocols, database schema, and stored data are
  unchanged. Manual actions, terminal streaming, and job rejection refreshes
  retain their existing behavior.
